obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system throughout the system's lifecycle.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data governance and quality criteria, including bias examination and mitigation.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, containing at least the Annex IV elements, before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it, including being able to disregard or override its output.
Design the system to achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout its lifecycle.
Carry out the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market.
Register yourself and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

key_facts: The tool screens and ranks job applicants' CVs.
It shortlists the top candidates for recruiters.
to_confirm: Confirm the tool is intended for recruitment or selection in the EU, or its output is used in the EU.
Confirm whether the tool is a safety component or otherwise falls under other Union product legislation. This is unlikely for a CV screener.

obligations.text: Design the chatbot so shoppers are told they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person.

key_facts: Customer-service chatbot on an e-commerce website
Answers shopper questions in natural language
Interacts directly with shoppers
to_confirm: The chatbot only answers shopper questions and does not make decisions such as credit or eligibility assessments, which could change the tier.
The chatbot does not generate synthetic content that would trigger separate marking duties.

obligations.text: Take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff who operate or use the system (no other mandatory obligations; voluntary codes of conduct are optional).

key_facts: AI spam filter
Sorts incoming company email into inbox or junk
to_confirm: The filter is used only for spam sorting and not to evaluate or monitor employees or to make decisions about people.

Develop the model using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.

key_facts: The model scores loan applicants' creditworthiness
The bank uses the score to decide who gets a loan
to_confirm: The system is used to score natural persons (consumers or individual applicants), not only businesses.
The system is not used solely to detect financial fraud.

obligations.text: Do not place this social scoring system on the market, put it into service or use it. The ban covers scoring that leads to detrimental treatment in unrelated social contexts or treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate, and no exception applies to denying public services on the basis of a behaviour score.

key_facts: Government system gives each citizen a trustworthiness score
The score is based on everyday behaviour
The score is used to grant or deny access to public services
to_confirm: Confirm that the denial of services is either in a context unrelated to where the behavioural data was collected or disproportionate to the behaviour. Both are likely on the facts described.

key_facts: The AI system evaluates students' exam answers.
It assigns the grades that decide whether students progress to the next year.
to_confirm: Confirm the system is intended to be used for the grading that decides progression, not only as a preparatory aid.
Confirm whether a human teacher reviews and can override the grades.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system throughout the system's lifecycle.
Develop the system on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria, where the system is trained on data.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, containing at least the Annex IV elements, before placing on the market or putting into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so that natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Design the system to achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and to perform consistently throughout its lifecycle.
Follow the internal-control conformity assessment procedure (Annex VI), with no notified body involved.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

key_facts: The AI assesses asylum seekers' applications
It flags a risk level for each applicant
Border officials receive the output
to_confirm: Confirm the system is used by or on behalf of competent public authorities, such as border or asylum officials.
Confirm that its use is permitted under relevant Union or national law, because Annex III point 7 applies only so far as that is the case.
Confirm the risk flag does not amount to a prohibited practice, for example profiling-based criminal risk prediction or biometric categorisation.

obligations.text: As provider, ensure the app's synthetic video outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
As deployer, disclose that the deep fake video content has been artificially generated or manipulated.

key_facts: The app generates realistic AI videos of real public figures
The videos show those figures saying things they never said
The videos are used for advertising campaigns
to_confirm: Whether the public figures have consented to use of their likeness. The Act does not remove national law duties on personality rights, data protection, advertising or consumer protection.
Whether any campaign could be used for election or political influence, or to deceive in ways that engage other rules.
Whether the content is evidently artistic, satirical or fictional, which would limit the disclosure duty to disclosing that the content exists in a way that does not hamper enjoyment of the work.

rows.clarifying_question: What is the specific intended purpose of the AI tool: what task does it perform, what data does it process, and who uses or acts on its output (for example, is it used for HR or employment decisions, credit assessments, customer chat, content generation, or something else)?

obligations.text: Ensure the system's synthetic image and text outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

If deployed content is a deep fake, disclose that it has been artificially generated or manipulated. Where the work is evidently creative or artistic, disclose in a way that does not hamper its display.

key_facts: The system generates marketing images and ad copy from a text brief
The output is intended for the company's social media
to_confirm: Whether you are the provider of the generator, or only a deployer using a third-party tool. The marking duty falls on the provider, and the disclosure duty falls on the deployer.
Whether any images depict realistic people, places or events and so would count as deep fakes.
Whether the ad copy is published to inform the public on matters of public interest. Ordinary marketing copy normally is not.

key_facts: Internal research model trained and tested in the lab only
Never placed on the market
Never used on real users
to_confirm: The model is never deployed internally for real operational use, which could count as putting it into service.
No testing in real-world conditions is planned.
Other Union law, such as GDPR, still applies to the research activity.

obligations.text: No mandatory obligations apply; the AI literacy duty and voluntary codes of conduct are optional good practice.

key_facts: The system only detects duplicate job applications.
A recruiter removes the duplicates.
It does not score, rank or evaluate candidates.
to_confirm: Confirm the system performs no profiling of natural persons, because profiling would make it high-risk regardless of the derogation.
Confirm that duplicate detection does not influence which candidates are advanced or rejected beyond removing exact duplicates.
A provider relying on the Art 6(3) derogation should document that assessment before placing the system on the market.

rows.clarifying_question: What specifically does the AI do in your hiring process (for example targeting job ads, filtering or ranking applications, scoring or evaluating candidates, scheduling), how is its output used, and who acts on it (for example a recruiter who decides, or an automatic rejection)?
key_facts: AI is used somewhere in the hiring process, with no further detail

Develop the system on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.

Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.

Deployers must use the system according to its instructions for use and assign human oversight to competent, trained and authorised people.
Deployers must inform applicants that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
Make sure applicants are told they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious.

key_facts: The system screens job applicants
It decides who advances to interview
It runs as a chatbot on a careers page
to_confirm: Confirm whether you are the provider (built the system) or only the deployer (use a third-party tool), as the obligations differ.
Confirm whether a human reviews or can override the interview-advancement decisions.

obligations.text: Do not place on the market, put into service for this purpose, or use an AI system that predicts the risk of a person committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits. The exception for supporting human assessment based on objective, verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity does not apply here.

key_facts: The system predicts how likely an individual is to commit a crime
It uses only personal traits and background
Police use it to decide who to watch
to_confirm: Confirm that no objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity feed the assessment, and that it is not only a support tool for a human assessment of a person's involvement in a specific criminal activity.

obligations.text: No mandatory obligations apply, but providers and deployers should take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of their staff (Art 4), and may follow voluntary codes of conduct.

key_facts: AI grammar and spell-checker
Suggests fixes while the user types in a word processor
to_confirm: Confirm the tool only corrects or suggests edits and does not generate substantial new text or substantially change the meaning of the user's text. If it did, Art 50(2) marking could apply.
Confirm it is not used for an Annex III purpose, for example grading exams or screening job applicants.

obligations.text: Do not place on the market, put into service or use real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement, unless and in so far as strictly necessary for a listed objective: (i) targeted search for abduction, trafficking or sexual exploitation victims or missing persons, (ii) preventing a specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or safety or a genuine terrorist threat, or (iii) locating or identifying a suspect of an Annex II offence punishable by at least four years' custody. The exceptions do not cover general, untargeted facial recognition of people in public squares.

key_facts: Real-time facial recognition of people in public squares
Output is streamed to the police
to_confirm: Whether any use is limited to one of the narrow objectives in Art 5(1)(h)(i)-(iii) and targeted at a specific individual.
Whether each use is authorised under national law, with a fundamental rights impact assessment and EU database registration as Art 5(2) requires.
Whether the recognition is truly real-time, as opposed to post-event.

obligations.text: Do not place this system on the market, put it into service for this purpose, or use it to infer employees' emotions in the workplace; the exception for medical or safety reasons does not apply to mood scoring in meetings.

key_facts: The tool reads employees' facial expressions during meetings
It scores employee mood, which means inferring emotions
The setting is the workplace
to_confirm: Check whether the tool is really intended for a medical or safety purpose. Nothing in the description suggests that it is.
Check whether the tool infers emotions from biometric data such as facial images.

The credit scores decide loan approvals
to_confirm: Confirm the scores are used to evaluate natural persons (consumers or individual applicants), not only companies.
Confirm the system is not used solely to detect financial fraud, which is the only exception in Annex III(5)(b).

obligations.text: Do not place on the market, put into service for this purpose, or use a biometric categorisation system that categorises individuals by biometric data to infer race, religious beliefs or similar attributes. The exceptions for labelling or filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets and for law-enforcement categorisation of biometric data do not apply to the described use.

key_facts: The tool does real-time biometric categorisation
It infers people's ethnicity and religion from their faces
to_confirm: Confirm the tool is not used only to label or filter lawfully acquired biometric datasets.
Confirm the tool is not used in the area of law enforcement, which the prohibition does not cover.
